assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, the Taylor rule and the microfounded policy-analysis apparatus, underlies modern central-bank practice. It combines conceptual influence with large policy consequences.
assessment.attribution: Taylor (staggered contracts, the policy rule), Woodford (the neo-Wicksellian monetary framework) and Gali (the canonical NK model and its empirical evaluation) form a defensible core. Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets also have strong claims, so any three-person cut leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1970s to the 2000s and has been tested through several decades of policy use and critique, including the post-2008 and post-2021 episodes. It is fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee would prefer a different three-person subset, such as one including Calvo, Christiano or Eichenbaum.
Post-2008 and post-2021 criticism of the representative-agent NK core may weigh against it.
The group is large and its credit is diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance opened a large empirical and conceptual research programme on how legal institutions and investor protection shape financial development and growth. Its influence on finance, corporate governance and comparative institutional analysis is very broad.
assessment.attribution: The core legal-origins and investor-protection papers are the joint work of La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. Vishny's contribution is more associated with the corporate governance survey and other collaborations with Shleifer. The three proposed names carry the legal-origins work most directly, but the four-way joint authorship makes a clean cut uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The work began in the late 1990s and has had more than two decades of replication, extension and critique.
uncertainties: Legal-origins identification and measurement have been criticised, and the empirical regularities may be seen as partly contested.
Shleifer's many other contributions, including behavioural finance and limits to arbitrage, could shift how the credit is framed.
Excluding Vishny may be judged an attribution problem.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade is modelled and measured. It established new gains-from-trade channels and a shared micro-level framework for empirical and quantitative trade work.
assessment.attribution: The Melitz (2003) model is the central contribution, and Helpman's work on heterogeneous firms and on trade and organization is closely connected to it. Redding has important quantitative extensions. Other contributors, such as Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, overlap with the broader literature but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The framework dates from the early 2000s and has been extensively applied and tested for more than 20 years.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee would credit empirical pioneers of firm-level trade facts who are not on this ballot.
Helpman's credit is also spread across other trade topics, as the separate trade-politics ballot shows.
The longlist's Ricardian trade candidate overlaps with this field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors built a systematic theoretical and empirical political economics of constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy. The work links institutions to economic outcomes, and the field is now central to economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clearest pair through their joint research programme and book. Besley's contributions on state capacity, accountability and public policy are substantial and complementary. The trio is reasonably coherent.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 1990 to the present, with major empirical and theoretical follow-up literatures and clear pedagogical influence.
uncertainties: Whether Besley's work is seen as sufficiently integral to the core programme or as a separate strand.
The Nobel was already awarded for institutions and growth (2024), so the Committee may weigh topical proximity.
Some causal claims about constitutional effects remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock and task-based analyses reshaped understanding of how trade and technology affect labour demand, regional adjustment and wage inequality. The work has had large academic and policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across both the task framework and the trade-shock papers. Dorn and Hanson are the main co-authors of the China-shock work. The task approach also depends on others, including Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Katz, so credit across the two strands is not clean.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from about 2003 to 2016. The empirical effects are well studied and have been debated and refined.
uncertainties: The task-model contributions of Acemoglu and others are not on this ballot, and the Committee may see this as a partial attribution.
Estimates of the China shock's magnitude and persistence are still debated.
The work is more recent and less settled than the strongest legacy candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles model explains how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It became a foundation of macro-finance and of post-crisis modelling of financial frictions.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are clearly credited for the core 1997 paper. Gertler and Gilchrist contributed to the financial accelerator, but that work is more closely tied to Bernanke, who has already been recognised for related research. Two names give a tighter and more defensible attribution.
assessment.maturity: The model dates from 1997 and has been extended and applied for decades, including in analysis of the 2008 crisis.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier recognition of Bernanke, Diamond and Dybvig for banks and financial crises.
A broader financial-accelerator framing could argue for including Gertler.
The Committee might want more direct empirical confirmation of the specific mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how an informed designer optimally shapes others' information. The framework has had broad influence across theory, mechanism design and applications.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow wrote the foundational persuasion paper. Bergemann and Morris developed information design and Bayesian correlated equilibrium. Choosing three of the four requires a judgement that could be disputed, and Morris also has wider contributions on global games and higher-order beliefs.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from 2011 and later, so it is comparatively young. It has had rapid uptake, but some applied validation and long-run influence remain unproven.
uncertainties: The attribution split between persuasion and information design is uncertain.
The work may be considered too recent for recognition.
Gentzkow's separate empirical work could dilute or complicate the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave the standard non-cooperative foundation for bargaining and a bridge to decentralized market trading. It is a core tool of game theory and economic theory.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein's 1982 paper is the key contribution. Rubinstein and Wolinsky (1985) extended it to markets. Binmore has related independent work on bargaining, but his role is more tied to the broader development and interpretation of the models.
assessment.maturity: The work is more than 40 years old. It is thoroughly established, widely taught, and has years of theoretical and experimental scrutiny.
uncertainties: Game theory has already been recognized several times, so the Committee may see the area as relatively covered.
The Committee may consider the contribution foundational but narrower than the larger empirical and macro agendas.
Binmore's potential claim to credit is not reflected in the proposed names.
